summary: Measured the six pilot_hull/pilot_gear samples with my own numpy code before reading the synth agent's module or report, then compared. My numbers agree with the agent's within rounding for every target in the brief (the only difference is the window: a Hann window on a 30 ms attack halves the share above 1 kHz, a rectangular window reproduces the agent's 61.5 %). No sound breaks a general rule: true peaks -1.2 dBFS or lower, DC below 1e-4, onset within 3.7 ms (at 1 % of peak), last 10 ms below -86 dBFS, no stray click, bass equal between channels, loudness equal inside each family within 0.1 LU. No must-fix. The weak point is the two listening models: CLAP puts hull_a and hull_b nearest 'taut plastic foil' (0.097, 0.217) and scores the gear_b and gear_c descriptions below zero with 'toy sound effect' above them; Qwen2-Audio called hull_a 'a liquid poured from a container', hull_b 'an electronic sound effect', hull_c 'a digital drum one shot', gear_a 'a door closing and a safe being locked' (a fair match), gear_b 'a space laser', gear_c 'an online game sound effect'. Verdicts: hull_a flag, hull_b flag, hull_c pass, gear_a pass, gear_b flag, gear_c flag. Only hull_c and gear_a look like what the brief describes by every instrument.

notVerified: Nothing was heard. All character judgements come from my own numbers, the six spectrogram PNGs, CLAP and one Qwen2-Audio answer per file; a listening test is still needed.

The hull_a partials list comes from simple peak picking on a Hann-windowed FFT and cannot separate detuned twins reliably (only 810/816 Hz was resolved), so 'at least twelve partials' and the pair detuning are confirmed only up to about 1.3 kHz; partials up to 5 kHz were not counted.

The rattle knocks of hull_a at 62, 105 and 170 ms were not isolated by my measurements. The check for identical repeated pings is by tick-height variation (cv 0.44, 0.54, 0.59) and the spectrograms, not by cross-correlating tick waveforms.
Onset is the first sample above 1 % of the file's peak; the gear files fade in and the rule says within 5 ms, other thresholds give other numbers.
Band shares use one FFT over the whole file or window (rectangular unless stated), not an octave filter bank; attack shares move a lot with the window (halved with a Hann window).

CLAP scores are uncalibrated cosine similarities of about 0.0-0.3 and Qwen2-Audio is a 7B model asked once per file; both are hints only. The CLAP run used my own script around the Clap class of tools/audio/listen/compare.py; describe.py ran once for all six files (mode bnb4, no memory failure).

Mixed-scene masking, small-speaker playback and a comparison against the owner's approved low boom were not tested. I read the agent's report and the brief only after measuring, and did not read its module.
